evidence.claim: GitHub says it collects account data such as handle, name, email address, password, payment and transaction information when you open an account.
GitHub says that if it detects a Global Privacy Control signal it will not share your data, and states that it does not sell your data.
GitHub says its analytics and advertising partners may use tracking technologies in its Services to collect personal information about online activities.
GitHub says you reserve the right to request deletion of your data, barring a few exceptions.
GitHub says it does not sell your data, but its analytics and advertising partners may use tracking technologies in its Services.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 1.276.0 (report dated Sept. 14, 2026) found code signatures for 2 known tracker SDK(s): Google CrashLytics (crash reporting), Google Firebase Analytics (analytics). A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.
